name: Demiurges Play Again
description: Demiurges Shambambukli and Mazukta love to watch the games of ordinary people. Today, they noticed two men who play the following game. There is a rooted tree on n nodes, m of which are leaves (a leaf is a nodes that does not have any children), edges of the tree are directed from parent to children. In the leaves of the tree integers from 1 to m are placed in such a way that each number appears exactly in one leaf. Initially, the root of the tree contains a piece. Two players move this piece in turns, during a move a player moves the piece from its current nodes to one of its children; if the player can not make a move, the game ends immediately. The result of the game is the number placed in the leaf where a piece has completed its movement. The player who makes the first move tries to maximize the result of the game and the second player, on the contrary, tries to minimize the result. We can assume that both players move optimally well. Demiurges are omnipotent, so before the game they can arbitrarily rearrange the numbers placed in the leaves. Shambambukli wants to rearrange numbers so that the result of the game when both players play optimally well is as large as possible, and Mazukta wants the result to be as small as possible. What will be the outcome of the game, if the numbers are rearranged by Shambambukli, and what will it be if the numbers are rearranged by Mazukta? Of course, the Demiurges choose the best possible option of arranging numbers.
input_specification: The first line contains a single integer n — the number of nodes in the tree ( 1 ≤ n ≤ 2·10 5 ). Each of the next n - 1 lines contains two integers u i and v i ( 1 ≤ u i , v i ≤ n ) — the ends of the edge of the tree; the edge leads from node u i to node v i . It is guaranteed that the described graph is a rooted tree, and the root is the node 1.
output_specification: Print two space-separated integers — the maximum possible and the minimum possible result of the game.
approach_summary: Define tree DP state dp[u][state] computing optimal subproblem values for the subtree rooted at u. Aggregate transitions across children in post-order traversal in O(N × S) time.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 538E — Demiurges Play Again [463. DP on Trees and DAGs]
topic_editorial.summary: Tree Dynamic Programming with post-order traversal.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: A rooted tree has a clean hierarchical structure: removing the root decomposes the tree into independent disjoint subtrees. Therefore, the optimal solution for a subtree rooted at vertex $u$ depends purely on the solutions of its direct children $v \in \text{children}(u)$.
topic_editorial.solution_walkthrough:
### Step 1: Root Selection & State Definition
Arbitrarily root the tree at node $1$. Define:
- $dp[u][0] = $ optimal value for the subtree of $u$ if node $u$ is excluded.
- $dp[u][1] = $ optimal value for the subtree of $u$ if node $u$ is included.

### Step 2: Post-Order DFS Traversal
We traverse the tree using depth-first search. A node $u$ computes its answers only after all its children $v \in \text{adj}[u]$ have computed theirs:
$$\text{dfs}(u, \text{parent})$$

### Step 3: Subtree Transition
For each child $v$ of $u$ ($v \ne \text{parent}$):
$$dp[u][0] = \sum_{v} \max(dp[v][0], dp[v][1])$$
$$dp[u][1] = \text{val}[u] + \sum_{v} dp[v][0]$$

### Step 4: Final Answer
At the root:
$$\text{Ans} = \max(dp[1][0], dp[1][1])$$
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
  Each node and edge in the tree is visited exactly once during the DFS traversal. All transitions at node $u$ run in time proportional to its degree. Summing across all vertices: $\sum \text{deg}(u) = 2(N-1) = \mathcal{O}(N)$.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
  Adjacency list storage takes $\mathcal{O}(N)$ memory, DP state arrays take $\mathcal{O}(N)$ memory, and the DFS call stack takes at most $\mathcal{O}(N)$ depth in the worst case.
